messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool `orchid-health-prod-1` GPU utilization critical (100%) - queue depth 1,200 - autoscaler unable to provision.

sre_alex: paging on-call, starting triage. tagging @oncall_jane

oncall_jane: I'm on it. pulling logs and pool state now.

infra_mike: checking metrics — allocation shows all 16 GPUs in pool pinned to tenant 'orchid-health' and 0 spare seats. Sustained enqueue rate up 3x in last 10m.

ml_ops_sana: models served: `redwood-7b-quant-v2` pinned for latency/quality. No automatic fallback configured for this tenant.

sre_alex: options: 1) temporary burst override into shared burst capacity (fast, risk of noisy neighbour) 2) spin up additional dedicated nodes (30-90m) 3) route non-critical routes to `redwood-3b-q` (immediate but quality hit) 4) throttle/queue enforcement on tenant (can preserve capacity for highest-priority calls).

cs_jordi: FYI CSM oncall confirms Orchid Health reports critical job failures for nightly ingestion. They've set P1 on their side.

oncall_jane: running quick checks:
```
# pool state
rpoolctl list --pool orchid-health-prod-1
POOL: orchid-health-prod-1  GPUs:16  Allocated:16  QueueDepth:1200  EnqueuedRate: 320/s
```

infra_mike: we can open a 30m burst override per policy if SRE lead signs off. It'll borrow from shared reserved capacity.

ml_ops_sana: immediate mitigation I'd push: apply routing fallback for background/ingestion routes to `redwood-3b-q` and keep interactive endpoints on 7b. Patch below:
```
{"routing_rules": [{"route":"/ingest/*","target":"redwood-3b-q","max_tokens":512}],"tenant":"orchid-health"}
```

sre_alex: propose: (A) approve 30m burst now, (B) apply routing fallback for ingestion, (C) enable per-tenant throttling at 50% for non-critical endpoints. Need explicit approval from @prod_priya or @infra_mike.

prod_priya: I approve burst for 30m. Also require throttling and fallback. :thumbsup: 

sre_alex: executing burst override:
```
dedicated-cli burst --tenant orchid-health --pool orchid-health-prod-1 --duration 30m --reason "prod outage - approve Priya"
```

deploy-bot: autoscaler: started provisioning 4 GPUs into orchid-health-prod-1 (requested by sre_alex)

infra_mike: GPUs came up +4, pool now 20 GPUs. queue depth 1200 -> 300 and dropping.

oncall_jane: applied routing fallback for `/ingest/*` and throttling rules. verifying.

ml_ops_sana: confirm: ingestion traffic now hitting 3b variant — p50 latency -> 180ms, quality OK for ingestion pipeline.

cs_jordi: Orchid Health oncall says ingestion back to steady state for now, but they saw some failures during the spike. They're asking for timeline and next steps.

sre_alex: current status: burst active, extra GPUs online, routing fallback in place, queue draining. Customer notified.

prod_priya: good — please open an incident postmortem and include root cause: why autoscaler didn't provision earlier and why tenant pinned all GPUs.

oncall_jane: will file the postmortem and create a follow-up JIRA to add an automatic fallback policy for dedicated tenants (configurable fallback to smaller model + auto-throttle) and to improve autoscaler signal thresholds.

sre_alex: owners: postmortem -> oncall_jane, autoscaler followup -> infra_mike, tenant-policy change -> ml_ops_sana, customer follow-up -> cs_jordi. ETA for PBIs in 2 business days.

infra_mike: leaving monitoring hooks for 2hr; will run a controlled drain after burst expires and reconcile billing/usage for burst.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: TIMEBEDGED: incident flagged resolved when queue < 50 and GPUs stable. Current queue=42. Pending burst expiry at +30m.

cs_jordi: I'll send a summary to Orchid Health and offer a scheduled call to review mitigations.

sre_alex: closing handoff. tagging for awareness: #eng-infra #eng-sre #eng-ml

oncall_jane: final note: commands used and logs saved to `incidents/1778203456` artifact bundle.
